title: ～たびに — “every time ～”
summary: Verb dictionary form or noun + の + たびに means “every time A happens, B also happens.” B is a reaction, feeling or change that occurs each time. It is used for repeated, regular occasions.

patterns.form: 動詞辞書形 ＋ たびに
patterns.gloss: dictionary form + たびに (見るたびに)

patterns.form: 名詞 ＋ の ＋ たびに
patterns.gloss: noun + の + たびに (旅行のたびに)

body.p: たび means “occasion, time.” 見るたびに is “each time I see (it).” Attach it to the dictionary form of a verb, or to a noun with の: 春が来るたびに, 旅行のたびに.
The second part is usually something that arises on its own: a feeling (思い出す, 懐かしくなる), a wish, or a change. It is natural for these things to happen automatically each time.
～たびに stresses that the same thing repeats at each occasion. It is slightly formal and often used in writing. In casual talk, 見ると、いつも... is also common.

examples.ja: この写真（しゃしん）を見（み）るたびに、母（はは）を思（おも）い出（だ）す。
examples.romaji: Kono shashin o miru tabi ni, haha o omoidasu.
examples.tr: Every time I see this photo, I remember my mother.

examples.ja: 春（はる）が来（く）るたびに、故郷（こきょう）の桜（さくら）を思（おも）い出（だ）す。
examples.romaji: Haru ga kuru tabi ni, kokyō no sakura o omoidasu.
examples.tr: Every time spring comes, I remember the cherry blossoms of my hometown.

examples.ja: この曲（きょく）を聞（き）くたびに、学生時代（がくせいじだい）に戻（もど）りたくなる。
examples.romaji: Kono kyoku o kiku tabi ni, gakusei jidai ni modoritaku naru.
examples.tr: Every time I hear this song, I want to go back to my school days.

pitfalls: With a noun, you need の: 旅行のたびに, not 旅行たびに.
Do not use it for a one-time event. It needs a situation that repeats.
